newsitem.title: USA: Blue Shield of Calif. settles Medicare claims case.
newsitem.headline: Blue Shield of Calif. settles Medicare claims case.

text.p: Blue Shield of California has agreed to pay $12 million to settle allegations it submitted false claims involving the federal Medicare program, two government agencies said on Friday.

The U.S. Justice Department and the Department of Health and Human Services said the agreement settles allegations in a civil lawsuit that Blue Shield covered up claims-processing errors from federal auditors. It had a contract to process and pay Medicare claims.
A year ago, Blue Shield pleaded guilty in federal court in Sacramento to three criminal charges of conspiracy and obstructing a federal audit. It paid a $1.5 million criminal fine in that case.

The $12 million settlement involved a separate whistleblower lawsuit initially brought by a former employee and then joined by the federal government. Under the settlement, the ex-employee will receive 18 percent of the total.

The lawsuit, filed in federal court in San Francisco, had alleged that employees in Blue Shield's Medicare division in Chico and Marysville, California, altered or discarded documents that would have disclosed the claims-processing errors and substituted backdated documents.
The Department of Health and Human Services said Blue Shield agreed to take steps to ensure future compliance with the Medicare rules.
